entries.name: Ernest Newell Weber

expected.convicted: Yes — contemporary participant account documents trial and sentence
expected.sentence: Tried and sentenced on June 6, 1961. Terry Sullivan’s first-person November 1961 account identifies Newell Weber as his fellow rider and says both served their full sentence, described as four-and-a-half months including fine time. The exact release date and individual prison-transfer dates remain unverified.

updates.sentence: Tried and sentenced on June 6, 1961. Terry Sullivan’s first-person November 1961 account identifies Newell Weber as his fellow rider and says both served their full sentence, described as four-and-a-half months including fine time. An FBI October 23, 1961 report explicitly records his release that day on expiration of sentence. Individual prison-transfer dates remain unverified.

entries.rationale: FBI report dated October 23, 1961, PDF page47, individually names Ernest Newell Weber as released that day on sentence expiration. Original visually verified.

entries.name: Harold Andrews

expected.charges: Freedom Ride participation — arrested Jackson, May 24, 1961.
expected.convicted: Unresolved — the arrest is documented; the disposition is not established in the CRDL record
expected.sentence: Arrested 1961-05-24. The Civil Rights Digital Library establishes the arrest and the identification photograph but not the disposition, any transfer to Parchman, or the release date — unresolved pending court, jail, or penitentiary records.

updates.sentence: Taken to jail after the May 24, 1961 Freedom Ride. Fellow rider Frank Holloway describes their confinement in Jackson city jail, Hinds County jail and the county penal farm, followed by release on $500 appeal bond to testify in Montgomery. Exact release date remains unresolved.

entries.rationale: Holloway firsthand account names Andrews throughout the journey, imprisonment and joint appeal-bond release. May24 booking already independently established; release not dated.

entries.name: Carl Miller

expected.charges: Unlawful assembly following the Franklin High School sit-in.
expected.sentence: Six months imposed; actual time served unverified.

updates.sentence: Released on personal recognizance April 5, 1968 after the initial April 4 detention. Later sentenced to six months and remanded in July; actual service and release from that later episode remain unverified.

entries.rationale: April6 Seattle Times page28 names Miller among those physically released shortly after4pm the previous day. Initial detention only; not a claim of full case duration including later July remand.

entries.name: Daniel Michael Lynem

expected.charges: Prosecution connected with the death of officer Nelson Sasscer.
expected.sentence: Held for one month after the June 5, 1969 arrest, according to his OC Weekly interview; the murder charges were dropped. Exact physical release date remains unresolved.

updates.sentence: Held June 5–July 3, 1969, when the murder charges were dismissed and he was released. The July 4 Santa Ana Register front page reports the Thursday dismissal and release and quotes Lynem expressing relief at being out.

entries.rationale: New original clipping refines previous one-month account: FridayJuly4 newspaper reports Thursdaydismissal/release and Lynem says glad he gotout. June5arrest in samearticle. Replace roundedmonth with exact28-day interval.
